_comment: Per-item overrides for Invoke-WsoContentTest.ps1 (see UEM-API-TESTING-SPEC.md). Keyed by the inventory Name column. Anything not listed here is tested with the defaults: a Script is expected to report Completed (exit 0) on every test device, a Sensor is expected to report a value that parses as its declared Data Type. Keys: skip (reason string: never tested), expect (Completed | Failed | NoResult, the last for a script that powers the device off before Hub can report, so no result within timeoutMinutes is the pass), variables (name -> value for $env:-backed parameters), match (regex the sensor value must satisfy), min / max (numeric bounds for Integer sensors), allowEmpty (true when an empty String value is acceptable), expectNoValue (true for a Boolean/DateTime sensor that emits nothing when its data source is absent; Hub rejects an empty typed value, so 'no value stored' is the pass condition on a device without the product), timeoutMinutes (per-item override of the wait for a result), onlyInGroup (smart group name; the item is skipped unless the run targets exactly that group, used for session-ending or network-severing scripts so the machine running the tool is never in scope), note (free text carried into the result file). Expectations marked 'lab VM' assume the disposable VMware lab build (no Wi-Fi, no Trellix, no SCOM, no Office). Revisit them on a product VM.

Invoke-SimpleReboot.ps1.note: Reboots the target 5 minutes after exit 0 (shutdown.exe /t 300). Only against the single-VM group so the machine running the tool is never in scope. Device-side proof: System event 1074 and uptime reset on CHASEWIN11_2.

Invoke-RebootWithUserDefer.ps1.note: Installs the deferral orchestrator task and exits 0; the prompt and eventual reboot happen later. Completed proves the install. Needs a signed-in user on CHASEWIN11_2 to see the toast; the deferral and forced reboot are then validated by hand (TEST-VALIDATION.md section 11).

DEX_Invoke-SignoffWindows.ps1.note: Logs every interactive session off the target at once. Hub runs as SYSTEM and reports after the logoff. Device-side proof: Winlogon event 7002 on CHASEWIN11_2.

DEX_Start-LockDeviceSoft.ps1.note: Disconnects the console session on the target with tsdiscon.exe, which lands on the lock screen. Needs a signed-in user on CHASEWIN11_2 to have any effect; exit 0 either way.

DEX_LockDevice-BitlockEncryptionActivate.note: Positive path: CHASEWIN11_2 has BitLocker on C: with a password protector (enabled 2026-10-30, no TPM, policy EnableBDEWithNoTPM). From v1.3.0 the script suspends the protectors, schedules the power-off 15 s out through shutdown.exe and exits 0, so Hub reports Completed with the manage-bde output before the device goes down. Afterwards boot the VM (no password prompt while suspended), confirm manage-bde -status C: shows Protection Off, then manage-bde -protectors -enable C:. On a device whose protection is not On, the script throws and exits 1 (Failed) without powering off; set expect to Failed to prove that guard (run c8e0dd on 1.1.0 showed the exit-code-only guard did not hold; run 534500 on 1.2.0 could only be judged as no result because of the in-process /t 0).

DEX_Stop-WindowsUpdate.ps1.note: Disables Windows Update and sets a 35-day pause on the device, so it only runs against the single-VM group after a snapshot. Revert the VM afterwards. Manual steps in TEST-VALIDATION.md 9.4.

DEX_Start-WindowsUpdate.ps1.note: Re-enables Windows Update and forces a scan/install through a scheduled task; the device may end up pending a restart. Single-VM group after a snapshot, run it last. Manual steps in TEST-VALIDATION.md 9.5.

Restart-WinProcessGracefulEx.ps1.note: Prototype 0.9.1 of the graceful restart, kept for reference. Same Chrome target as Restart-WinProcessGraceful.ps1; needs Chrome open in the signed-in session on CHASEWIN11_2. Single-VM group because it closes the user's browser.

Measure-LogonDurationMultiSession.ps1.skip: 87,435 characters, far over the UEM 32,767 limit, so the create call is refused. Test it by hand as SYSTEM on the lab VM (RunNow mode) per TEST-VALIDATION.md.

Start-UserProfileCleanup.ps1.note: Deletes local (non-enrollment) profiles unused for more than 30 days with hard-coded tunables and no dry-run mode, so only against the snapshotted single VM. On CHASEWIN11_2 no profile meets the age threshold, so Completed proves the enumeration and the no-delete path; the deletion path needs a planted stale profile and is a manual test (General-Testing-Guide.md 2.2).

Invoke-AutoRemediateNetworkStack.ps1.note: Resets adapters and Winsock on the target, which drops its network for a while; Hub reports once connectivity returns, hence the longer wait. Only against the single-VM group. Also covered by its break test on the lab VM.

Start-DefenderFullScan.ps1.note: Start-MpScan -AsJob returns at once, so the script completes in seconds, but the full scan then runs for hours on the device. Single-VM group after a snapshot so the sweep devices are not slowed. Manual steps in TEST-VALIDATION.md 4.7.

Invoke-AutoRemediateSCOMAgent.ps1.skip: Reference copy only: 48,336 characters exceeds the UEM 32,767 limit and the create call will be refused. Parts 1-3 are the deployable split.

Restart-WinService.ps1.note: Print Spooler exists on every Windows build and restarts cleanly.

Restart-WinProcess.ps1.note: High impact: run with -IncludeHighImpact. Target chosen 2026-10-30: Chrome is on the lab VMs and supports both the blunt and the graceful restart. Exits 0 when no matching process is running, so a device without Chrome open passes trivially; the device-side proof is Chrome's PIDs changing. Under UEM the relaunch runs as SYSTEM in session 0, so the user does not see the new window; that is a design limitation to record, not a test failure.

Restart-WinProcessGraceful.ps1.note: High impact: run with -IncludeHighImpact. Dispatch-only script: Completed proves the watchdog task was registered and started. The outcome is in %ProgramData%\AirWatch\Extensions\ProcessGraceful (watchdog.log, result.json); from 2.2.0 the next launcher run mirrors it into the DEXRecords key as LastResult* values, so a second run shows the first run's outcome. Chrome must be open on the device for anything to happen.

Invoke-AutoRemediateSCOMAgentPart1.ps1.skip: Deferred 2026-10-30: SCOM agent remediation is out of scope while the approach is reviewed (an agent upgrade is often the preferred fix).

Invoke-AutoRemediateSCOMAgentPart2.ps1.skip: Deferred 2026-10-30: SCOM agent remediation is out of scope while the approach is reviewed.

Invoke-AutoRemediateSCOMAgentPart3.ps1.skip: Deferred 2026-10-30: SCOM agent remediation is out of scope while the approach is reviewed.

Invoke-AutoRemediateDriverIssues.ps1.note: Filter matches the VMware devices on the lab VM. Scan/Restart only by default; the escalation chain is covered by the unit tests and break tests.

Invoke-DriverUpdates.ps1.note: Detect mode exits 1 whenever any driver update is offered, which UEM shows as Failed. The no-match filter pins exit 0 and proves the variables reach the script. Install mode is a manual test (TEST-VALIDATION.md 5.2).

Invoke-AutoRemediateWiFiSignalIssues.ps1.note: Lab VM has no Wi-Fi adapter, so step 1 fails by design and the script exits 1. Remove this expectation on a device with a wireless adapter.

Invoke-TrellixRefreshPolicies.ps1.note: Throws 'CmdAgent.exe was not found' without Trellix installed. Pins the guard on the lab VM; remove on a Trellix device.

Invoke-TrellixLocalUpdate.ps1.note: Without Trellix both executables are reported as not found and the script exits 0. Completed on the lab VM proves only the skip path.

Invoke-CrowdStrikeServiceRemediation.ps1.note: No Falcon on the lab VM; Completed proves only the 'nothing to remediate' path. Fixed 2026-10-29.

Invoke-TrendMicroServiceRemediation.ps1.note: No Trend Micro on the lab VM; Completed proves only the not-found path.

Invoke-AutoRemediateOutlook.ps1.note: Classic Outlook 16.0.18925 is on CBRADLEYSWIN11 since 2026-11-02 (outlook.com IMAP profile), so that device takes the product path; CHASEWIN11_2 has no Office and proves the [Skipped] path. Watch the run time: two lab runs took over 100 s, the time spent before the script's first line while the host was busy (TEST-VALIDATION.md 13.2.s); 1.1.1 bounds the step 3 event query. 1.1.2 reads the Application log through the .NET EventLogReader: proven in run 4ea50e (2026-11-05), step 3 reported 2 Outlook error events on CBRADLEYSWIN11 where every earlier Hub run had failed the query. Published timeout is 30 s.

Invoke-AutoRemediateTeams.ps1.note: New Teams (MSTeams 26276.x) is on CBRADLEYSWIN11 since 2026-11-02, so that device takes the product path; CHASEWIN11_2 has no Teams and proves the [Skipped] path. Device-side proof: DEXRecords TeamsErrors on CBRADLEYSWIN11.

Invoke-AutoRemediateZoom.ps1.note: Zoom 7.2.5 is installed machine-wide on CBRADLEYSWIN11 since 2026-11-05 (Program Files, no App Paths entry), so that device takes the product path from 1.0.2 on (1.0.1 misdetected it as not installed, 13.2.dd); CHASEWIN11_2 has no Zoom and proves the [Skipped] path. Device-side proof: DEXRecords ZoomErrors with ZoomVersion and TotalSteps 5.

Set-LocationServices.ps1.note: Action script (new 2026-11-05, 1.0.1). The default case runs Enable with WhatIf, so both lab VMs report their current device and user values and change nothing. A real Enable or Disable run proves the effect: read HKLM and HKU ConsentStore\location Value on the device afterwards. Exit 1 means bad input, not elevated, or a failed write.

Invoke-AutoRemediateOfficeAddins.ps1.note: Suite-wide Office add-in script (new 2026-11-05, 1.0.0): twelve steps, two per application, for Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Access, OneNote and Publisher. Office 365 C2R 16.0.18925 is on CBRADLEYSWIN11, so that device takes the product path; CHASEWIN11_2 has no Office and proves the [Skipped] path. Device-side proof: DEXRecords OfficeAddinsErrors with TotalSteps 12. Report-only by default; AllowDestructiveActions and ReenableDisabledItems are the gates.

Invoke-AutoRemediateWord.ps1.note: Office 365 C2R is on CBRADLEYSWIN11 (product path, 7 steps from 1.0.3: add-in steps moved to Invoke-AutoRemediateOfficeAddins.ps1); CHASEWIN11_2 has no Office and proves the [Skipped] path. Device-side proof: DEXRecords WordErrors. Report-only by default apart from creating a missing AutoRecover folder.

Invoke-AutoRemediateExcel.ps1.note: Office 365 C2R is on CBRADLEYSWIN11 (product path, 5 active steps from 1.0.3); CHASEWIN11_2 proves the [Skipped] path. 31,436 characters: under the 32,767 limit, over the 30,000 planning ceiling (documented exception). Device-side proof: DEXRecords ExcelErrors.

Invoke-AutoRemediatePowerPoint.ps1.note: Office 365 C2R is on CBRADLEYSWIN11 (product path, 4 active steps from 1.0.3); CHASEWIN11_2 proves the [Skipped] path. A real igd10iumd64.dll crash on CBRADLEYSWIN11 makes steps 2 and 6 Warn until about 2026-11-10. Device-side proof: DEXRecords PowerPointErrors.

Invoke-AutoRemediateAccess.ps1.note: Office 365 C2R is on CBRADLEYSWIN11 (product path, 3 active steps from 1.0.3); CHASEWIN11_2 proves the [Skipped] path. Device-side proof: DEXRecords AccessErrors.

Invoke-AutoRemediateOneNote.ps1.note: Office 365 C2R desktop OneNote is on CBRADLEYSWIN11 (product path, 3 active steps from 1.0.3); CHASEWIN11_2 proves the [Skipped] path. Device-side proof: DEXRecords OneNoteErrors.

Invoke-AutoRemediatePublisher.ps1.note: Office 365 C2R Publisher is on CBRADLEYSWIN11 (product path, 2 active steps from 1.0.3); CHASEWIN11_2 proves the [Skipped] path. Device-side proof: DEXRecords PublisherErrors.

Invoke-AutoRemediateAppXBloat.ps1.note: Deprovisions consumer inbox AppX packages on the test device. Expected and acceptable on a disposable VM; the first run changes the image.

Enable-HardwareAcceleratedGPUScheduling..note: Exits 1 on the run that enables HwSchMode (no re-detect) and 0 on every later run. A Failed verdict on a fresh device is expected once; re-run to confirm.

Invoke-RemediatePageFile.ps1.note: Exits 1 (Warning) when the page file is manually sized but under threshold, or system-managed with high usage. On the lab VM the page file is system-managed, so Completed is expected.

Invoke-AutoRemediateTimeSync.ps1.note: Both lab VMs are workgroup devices with an NTP peer, so step 2 is a Warning (ConfigureWorkgroupNtp defaults to false) and steps 1, 3 and 4 act only if W32Time is stopped, unsynchronised or skewed. Exits 1 only when a resolution block throws. Device-side proof: DEXRecords SystemHealth\TimeSync and UEM_AutoRemediateTimeSync.log; a resync shows as Clock Synchronization -> Remediated.

Invoke-AutoRemediateBitLockerProtection..note: CBRADLEYSWIN11 has no encrypted volume, so it proves only the no-volume exit 0. CHASEWIN11_2 has BitLocker on C: with a password protector (since 2026-10-30), so it takes the product path: if protection was left suspended by the lock-script tests the script resumes it, otherwise every step passes. Exits 1 when Get-BitLockerVolume fails (not elevated); Hub runs as SYSTEM so that should not happen. Device-side proof: DEXRecords SystemHealth\BitLockerProtection.

Invoke-AutoRemediateCertEnrollment.ps1.note: Off-domain lab VMs: step 5 reports not applicable, steps 2 to 4 report on the machine store. The CertificateServicesClient tasks are read through the Task Scheduler COM API (1.0.1), the first use of that path under Hub's PowerShell 7 as SYSTEM. Device-side proof: DEXRecords SystemHealth\CertEnrollment.

Start-ClearRecycleBin.ps1.note: Empties every user's Recycle Bin on the test device. Keep the test smart group to disposable VMs.

Invoke-AutoRemediateSCOMHealthServiceCac.skip: Deferred 2026-10-30: SCOM agent remediation is out of scope while the approach is reviewed. (Also: no SCOM agent on the lab VM.)

Invoke-AutoRemediateSCOMClonedIdentity.p.skip: Deferred 2026-10-30: SCOM agent remediation is out of scope while the approach is reviewed. (Also: no SCOM agent on the lab VM.)

Invoke-AutoRemediateSCOMMonitoringHost.p.skip: Deferred 2026-10-30: SCOM agent remediation is out of scope while the approach is reviewed. Launcher plumbing was proven under UEM in run 37acca (payload reached Skipped:NoAgent); keep that evidence.

sensor-getservice.ps1.skip: Sample only: emits the JSON list of every running service (about 2.4 KB). UEM stores at most 1 KB per sensor value and Hub drops the sample ('output length is greater than 1KB length', seen 2026-10-29).

Get-UserProfileSize.ps1.skip: Not sensor-shaped: writes 34 lines of log text, references an undefined CustomPSObject type and exits 1. Hub rejected it as 'failed sanity' on 2026-10-29. Needs a rewrite that emits one value before it can be a sensor.

performance_defender_scanorupdateactive..note: Hub rejected 1.0.0 as 'failed sanity' on both lab devices (2026-10-29) while an interactive run printed Idle. 1.0.1 silences the Get-WinEvent error stream; confirmed Idle on both devices in run 0501f4. 1.0.2 (2026-11-05) reads the Defender log through the .NET EventLogReader, so the full-scan branch is live under Hub for the first time (every Get-WinEvent form failed there, so 1.0.1 could only ever fall back to Get-MpComputerStatus).

logon_folder_redirection_map.ps1.note: Payload was ~1.2 KB and Hub dropped it as over 1 KB on 2026-10-29; the tenant's own published copy fails the same way on every sample. Restructured the same day (redirected targets plus local folder names); confirmed stored on both devices in run 0501f4, NoResult in e505e2 (Hub timing), stored again in 25a553 on 2026-11-05.

logon_folder_redirection_latency_probe.p.note: Payload was ~2.5 KB and Hub dropped it as over 1 KB on 2026-10-29. Restructured the same day (probe details only for redirected folders); confirmed stored on both devices in run 0501f4, NoResult in e505e2 (Hub timing), stored again in 25a553 on 2026-11-05.

logon_time.ps1.note: Passed with a value on both devices in run e5d833 (2026-11-05) once collector 1.1.3 had run under Hub (d17a02); before that the cache held LogonTime = Unknown and the sensor emitted nothing.

logon_gp_duration_ms.ps1.note: -2 (not applicable) on the workgroup lab VMs from collector 1.1.4: no user GP cycle inside the logon window and the device is not domain-joined. Earlier 40/70 ms values came from a refresh cycle ten minutes after logon (run 8c7790 probe, TEST-VALIDATION.md 8.3). A domain-joined device returns the real logon processing time.

logon_shell_ready_time.ps1.note: Passed with a value on both devices in run b9b16e (2026-11-05) once collector 1.1.4 took shell-ready from the session's explorer.exe creation time; before that the Winlogon 7001 filter never matched on Windows 11 and the sensor emitted nothing.

logon_gp_start_time.ps1.note: No value on the workgroup lab VMs by design from collector 1.1.4: the Group Policy 4001 is now bounded to the logon window, and a probe of the GP log under Hub (run 8c7790, 2026-11-05) showed these devices log their user 4001/8001 pairs only as later refresh cycles (ten minutes after logon and on Hub syncs), never at logon. The value e5d833 returned earlier was one of those refreshes. Passes with a value on a domain-joined device.

vpn_last_connect_time.ps1.note: No VPN client on the lab VMs, so the cache has no LastConnectTime and the DateTime sensor emits nothing by design.

vpn_dns_configured.ps1.note: Documented: no value is emitted without an active tunnel, because false would read as a real finding.

scom_management_server_reachable.ps1.note: No SCOM agent on the lab VMs; the sensor returns without output when AgentInstalled is absent.

scom_healthservice_running_standalone.ps.note: No SCOM agent root on the lab VMs; the sensor returns without output by design.

vpn_adapter_name.ps1.note: Empty by design without a VPN adapter (lab VMs).

vpn_health_reason.ps1.note: Empty by design when the VPN cache has no HealthReason (lab VMs).

scom_agent_health_reason.ps1.note: Since 2026-11-05 the reader names the no-cache case (NoAgentInstalled on the lab VMs) instead of emitting an empty string, which Hub drops.

scom_agent_version.ps1.note: Empty by design without a SCOM agent (lab VMs).

scom_agent_version_standalone.ps1.note: Empty by design without a SCOM agent (lab VMs).

Disable-NonEssentialStartupApps.ps1.note: 2.0.0 (2026-11-06). The default case runs with WhatIf so the sweep lists every startup entry of the console user with its facts (launch ms, signer, target present, StartupApproved state) and changes nothing; the disable path is proven by the break test. Device-side proof: HKLM\Software\AirWatch\Extension\DEXRecords\StartupApps with one Entry_<name> line per entry and DisabledCount 0 under WhatIf. Exit 0 after a fixing run; 1 only when a disable fails.

startup_apps_health.ps1.note: One-time JSON sensor, companion of Disable-NonEssentialStartupApps.ps1 2.0.0. Under Hub's 1 KB cap by construction (794 and 819 bytes on CBRADLEYSWIN11, 2026-11-06). Under SYSTEM it reports on the console user.
